This is the part that is labeled `Action Information area` in the specification.

It contains
```
  ActionCount
  ActionNameLengthBytes [0]
  ActionName [0]
  ActionPathLengthBytes [0]
  ...
  ActionNameLengthBytes [N]
  ActionName [N]
  ActionPathLengthBytes [N]
```
It is also returned in the `pldm_platform_redfish_action_pdr.action_info`.

I think I find it lacking that in case of the foreach API that we implement there is no easy way to get `ActionCount` without full iterating.

What is preffered way to add this?
1) add `uint8_t action_count` to the pdr structure
2) add `uint8_t action_count` to the action_info structure
3) create another API to get it from the `action_info` structure

The easiest way is 1/2, in case we do that, do we need to move `area.ptr` after the `ActionCount` field, or can we leave things as they are?

This represents the same information twice? `iter` also (conceptually) contains a count (`entries`) and a `struct variable_field`.

The only concern is loss of information during iteration. But perhaps people wanting to iterate multiple times could either dynamically store the results from the first iteration, or re-decode the message buffer?

> The only concern is loss of information during iteration

Yes, I thought we need to save it, so we can iterate multiple times.

This iterator API is kinda new to me, I don't have any experience for designing or using such things, but here are some thoughts to your suggestions.

> But perhaps people wanting to iterate multiple times could either dynamically store the results from the first iteration or re-decode the message buffer?

To me it looks like going all over the full PDR again seems like a too expensive move. And it is not very intuitive for the user, that iteration can be performed only once on data.

I remember I've once asked you, is it okay, that we need to write that much of a boilerplate code in the library to implement this iterator api. And you've answered that you don't mind having it, as long as API for the user is simple. I guess that idea stick with me. I think we shouldn't require the user to perform additional actions to make parsing permanent. It is not very obvious and gives some burden to the user, and the main point was to simplify things for the user.
Sure, my query wasn't a direction to change it, more just to discuss such thoughts. Thanks for your input. I'll think about it more.
Things were simplified according to the https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/libpldm/+/88328/

If we're storing this then perhaps we don't need the two `info` arguments to `decode_pldm_platform_redfish_action_pdr()`? We could initialise the `info`s later with the information from an instance of this struct?

I guess we can do something like that, but I don't think it would be fair/safe to ask the user to manually copy some fields from the `pldm_platform_redfish_action_pdr` to `pldm_platform_redfish_action_pdr_action_info`. So in this case we would need to introduce another API function to initialize the `pldm_platform_redfish_action_pdr_action_info` from  the `pldm_platform_redfish_action_pdr`. And I'm not sure that will simplify things
